message.content: ATP synthase (also known as Complex V or F₀F₁-ATPase) is the enzyme complex in mitochondria that synthesizes ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate (Pi). It uses the proton gradient generated by the electron transport chain (ETC) across the inner mitochondrial membrane. Protons flow back into the matrix through the F₀ portion of ATP synthase, driving rotation of its central stalk. This mechanical rotation is transmitted to the catalytic F₁ domain, where it induces conformational changes that enable the binding of ADP and Pi and their subsequent phosphorylation to form ATP. In short, ATP synthase converts the energy stored in the proton motive force into chemical energy stored in ATP, which is then used by the cell for various metabolic processes.
